    THR · X
    Entertainment magazine
    Valerie Perrine, known for her performances in 'Superman' and 'Lenny,' has died following a years-long battle with Parkinson's disease. She was 82. A GoFundMe has been created for Valerie to help cover the costs of her funeral because her "finances are exhausted," according to filmmaker Stacey Souther. "She faced Parkinson’s disease with incredible courage and compassion, never once complaining," Stacey wrote in a social media post today. "She was a true inspiration who lived life to the fullest — and what a magnificent life it was. The world feels less beautiful without her in it." (📸: Getty Images)

    90+ likes · 10 hours ago
    ABC · X
    Television network
    Valerie Perrine, best known for playing Miss Teschmacher in Superman and earning an Oscar nomination for Lenny, has passed away at 82. Her friend confirmed she died after a long battle with Parkinson’s disease, which she was diagnosed with in 2015. Perrine delivered a standout performance in Lenny (1974), earning a Best Actress Oscar nomination, and later became a fan favorite in Superman (1978) and Superman II. She also appeared in What Women Want, The Electric Horseman, and dozens of TV series throughout her career. A Texas-born actress who rose from Las Vegas showgirl to Hollywood star, Perrine leaves behind a decades-long legacy across film and television. Rest in peace 🕊️
